title: Large-scale geometry of the derived space: continuum limits, dimension, betweenness and geodesics

key_results.statement: For the square family $K_{h_{(i,j)}}=\tfrac in X+\tfrac jnY$ with $\sigma_X=\sigma_Y=\sigma$ and $\operatorname{Cov}_\chi(X,Y)=0$: $d_0(h_{(i,j)},h_{(i',j')})=\tfrac\sigma n\sqrt{(\Delta i)^2+(\Delta j)^2}$.

For the square family, $(X_n,d_0)$ converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to the Euclidean square $([0,\sigma]^2,|\cdot|_2)$, which is continuum-like, flat, of dimension 2 and isotropic; betweenness is the straight segment and the geodesic is unique.

For the square family at small $\lambda$ the neighbour graph $N_0$ is the square grid graph: $h_{(i,j)}\sim h_{(i',j')}$ iff $|\Delta i|+|\Delta j|=1$; ties violate the hypotheses of (11.11), so (4.3) is decided directly.
For the square family, $\ell_0=\tfrac\sigma n(|\Delta i|+|\Delta j|)$, and $(X_n,\ell_0)$ converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to the taxicab square $Y_b=([0,\sigma]^2,\|\cdot\|_1)$.
The limit $Y_b$ is a compact length space of dimension 2, so the square family under $\ell_0$ is continuum-like; it is not isotropic, because the unit ball of $\|\cdot\|_1$ is a square.

For the square family the $\ell_0$-shortest chains are the monotone lattice paths, $\binom{|\Delta i|+|\Delta j|}{|\Delta i|}$ in number (a single geodesic under $d_0$ in the limit); under $\ell_0$ in the limit the between points form the axis-parallel box; at small $\lambda$ the $\ell$-geodesics are among these chains, all of them if $[X,Y]=0$.
For the square family, $\max\ell_0/d_0=\sqrt2\approx1.414$, with equality iff $|\Delta i|=|\Delta j|\ge1$.

For the qubit disc family, $\alpha(h,h';\lambda)$ is the great-circle distance on the round sphere of radius $1/2$ between $F_\lambda(x_h,y_h)$ and $F_\lambda(x_{h'},y_{h'})$, where $F_\lambda(r,\phi)$ lies at arc length $\lambda r$ from $N=[\lvert0\rangle]$ on the meridian of azimuth $\phi-\pi/2$.

For the qubit disc family at fixed $\lambda$, $(X_n,\alpha)$ converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to the closed cap $\{\alpha(N,\cdot)\le\lambda r_0\}$ of the sphere of radius $1/2$ if $\lambda r_0<\pi/2$, and to the whole sphere $\mathbb{CP}^1$ if $\lambda r_0\ge\pi/2$; dimension 2, Gaussian curvature 4, geodesics are great-circle arcs; the limit is a length space (continuum-like) iff $\lambda r_0\le\pi/4$ or $\lambda r_0\ge\pi/2$.
For the compact windows ($m\ge2$) and $\lambda\in(0,\pi/2)$: $\alpha(h_i,h_j)=\alpha_k:=\arccos\bigl((\cos\lambda)^{2k}\bigr)$ with $k=\min(|i-j|,m)$, and $0<\alpha_1<\dots<\alpha_m<\pi/2$.
For the compact windows ($m\ge2$) and every $\lambda\in(0,\pi/2)$: $h_i\sim h_j$ iff $|i-j|=1$ or $|i-j|\ge2m-1$; the long edges come from ties at saturation.

For the compact windows with $n\ge2m$ and $A=n-2m+1$: the step counts $\eta^{\mathrm R}_k=\max(0,k-A)$ and $\eta^{\mathrm L}_k=\max(0,2m-k)$ to a place with a rightward, respectively leftward, jump, and for a pair $i<j$ the combinations $E_2=\min(\eta^{\mathrm R}_i+\eta^{\mathrm R}_j,\ \eta^{\mathrm L}_i+\eta^{\mathrm L}_j)$ and $E_3=\min(\eta^{\mathrm R}_i+\eta^{\mathrm L}_j,\ \eta^{\mathrm L}_i+\eta^{\mathrm R}_j)$.

For the compact windows with $r=|i-j|$ and $\lambda\in(0,\pi/2)$, exact for every $n$: $\ell=r\alpha_1$ if $n\le2m-1$; $\ell=\alpha_m$ if $r\ge2m-1$; $\ell=\min\{r\alpha_1,\ \alpha_m+(2m-1-r)\alpha_1,\ 2\alpha_m+E_2\alpha_1,\ 3\alpha_m+E_3\alpha_1\}$ if $n\ge2m$ and $1\le r\le2m-2$, with $E_2,E_3$ from (22.30); for $n\ge6m-4$ the minimum reduces to $\min\{r\alpha_1,\ \alpha_m+(2m-1-r)\alpha_1,\ 2\alpha_m\}$.

For the compact windows with $n\ge2m$, $w=4m-1-n$ and $\zeta=\alpha_m/\alpha_1$: the maximum $h_n(r)$, over pairs at index distance $r$, of $e=\min(E_2,\zeta+E_3)$ (the excess of the shortest chain with at least two jumps over $2\alpha_m$, in units of $\alpha_1$) is $\max\{0,C_{\mathrm{LR}},C_{\mathrm{MR}},C_{\mathrm{MM}}\}$ with the explicit candidates of (22.31); $h_n\equiv0$ for $n\ge6m-4$.

Exact diameter for the compact windows ($m\ge2$, $\lambda\in(0,\pi/2)$): $\operatorname{diam}(X_n,\ell)=(n-1)\alpha_1$ for $n\le2m-1$, and $\max_{1\le r\le2m-2}\min\{r\alpha_1,\ \alpha_m+(2m-1-r)\alpha_1,\ 2\alpha_m+h_n(r)\alpha_1\}$ for $n\ge2m$, with explicit closed forms for $n=2m$ and $n\ge6m-4$; for all $n$ it is at most $(2m-2)\alpha_1$.
For the compact windows ($m\ge2$), every $\lambda\in(0,\pi/2)$ and every choice of scales $s_n$, neither $(X_n,\ell/s_n)$ nor $(X_n,\ell_0/s_n)$ is continuum-like.

For exponential tails $\kappa(s)=q^{|s|}$, $0<q<1$ (infinite medium as the limit of long finite chains), with $r=|i-j|$ and $\beta=\tfrac{1+q^2}{1-q^2}$: $d_0(h_i,h_j)=\sqrt{2[\beta(1-q^r)-rq^r]}$, strictly increasing in $r$ and saturating at $\sqrt{2\beta}$, with $d_0(1)=\rho_1=\sqrt{2(1-q)/(1+q)}$.
For exponential tails at small $\lambda$ the neighbour graph $N_0$ is the path: $h_i\sim h_j$ iff $|i-j|=1$; on a line there are no ties, so (11.11) applies.
For exponential tails, $\ell_0(h_i,h_j)=\rho_1|i-j|$ with $\rho_1=\sqrt{2(1-q)/(1+q)}$.

For exponential tails, $(X_n,\ell_0/n)$ converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to the segment $([0,\rho_1],|\cdot|)$: continuum-like with $s_n=n$, of dimension 1; betweenness is the index order and the geodesic (shortest chain) is unique.

For exponential tails the margins in $d_0$ that decide the missing edges ($r\ge2$) are exponentially small in $r$: with $s=\lceil r/2\rceil$, the largest (midpoint witness) is $\delta(r)\sim(s+\beta)q^{s}/\sqrt{2\beta}$ and the smallest (neighbouring witness) is $\Delta(r)\sim(1-q)rq^{r-1}/\sqrt{2\beta}$ as $r\to\infty$; the edges ($r=1$) rest on the margin $d_0(2)-d_0(1)=O(1)$.

For the square grid with exponential tails $q^{|l_1-p_1|+|l_2-p_2|}$, $0<q<1$ (infinite medium as the limit of large finite grids), and $r_k=|p_k-p'_k|$: $d_0(h_p,h_{p'})=\Phi(r_1,r_2)=\sqrt{2[\beta^2-q^{r_1+r_2}(r_1+\beta)(r_2+\beta)]}$, symmetric and strictly increasing in each argument.

For the square grid with exponential tails at small $\lambda$ the neighbour graph $N_0$ is the square grid graph on $\{1,\dots,n\}^2$; ties violate the hypotheses of (11.11), so every pair is decided directly from (4.3).
For the square grid with exponential tails, $\ell_0(h_p,h_{p'})=\rho(|\Delta_1|+|\Delta_2|)$, where every edge has length $\rho=\Phi(1,0)=\tfrac{\sqrt{2(1+q^2)}}{1+q}$.

For the square grid with exponential tails, $(X_n,\ell_0/n)$ converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to $([0,1]^2,\rho\|\cdot\|_1)$: continuum-like of dimension 2; betweenness is the axis-parallel box, geodesics are all coordinate-monotone curves (unique iff the points lie on an axis-parallel line), and the limit is not isotropic.

For the square grid with exponential tails and $\lambda<\lambda_n$, all grid edges have the same $\alpha_e(\lambda)$, so $\ell=\|\Delta\|_1\alpha_e(\lambda)$ and the number of $\ell$-geodesics equals the number of $\ell_0$-shortest chains, $\binom{|\Delta_1|+|\Delta_2|}{|\Delta_1|}$.

For one fixed $\Gamma$-periodic pattern with finitely many edge orbits, independent of $n$ (F1), on domains $X_n=\pi^{-1}(nB)$ with $B$ compact convex (F2), and with recomputed neighbour graphs equal to the induced subgraphs and $d_n\le d_\infty+C'$ (F3): the rescaled $\ell_0$ never converges to an isotropic limit, because the limit norm is the polygonal stable norm of (P1)–(P2); if the pattern's graph is disconnected there is no limit. Patterns that change with $n$ are treated separately, and truncations that create new edges are not covered.

For patterns that change with $n$ (F1'), whose quotient graphs have at most $E_0$ edges with $E_0$ independent of $n$, with (F2')–(F3') and the uniformity (F4) (stable-norm defect, boundary constant and covering radius all $o(s_n)$): every two-dimensional limit of $(X_n,\ell_0/s_n)$ has a polygonal norm with at most $2^{E_0+1}$ vertices, so it is not isotropic.

For the line-arrangement family (lines $\langle a_j,p\rangle=m$, $m\in\mathbb Z$, for $k$ directions $\theta_j=\pi j/k$ with $a_j\in\mathbb Z^2$ the rounding of $k(\cos\theta_j,\sin\theta_j)$; places: regions $R$ meeting the interior of $nB$; one qubit cell per line meeting $nB$; records $K_{h_R}=\sum_L[R\subseteq L^+]\,\sigma_x^{[L]}$): $\cos\alpha(h_R,h_{R'};\lambda)=(\cos\lambda)^{d_G(R,R')}$ and $d_0(h_R,h_{R'})=\sqrt{d_G(R,R')}$, where $d_G(R,R')$ is the number of lines separating $R$ and $R'$, equal to their distance in the region graph on $X_n$.

For the line-arrangement family and every $\lambda\in(0,\pi/2)$: $N_V=G_k[X_n]$, $\ell=\lambda\,d_G$ and $\ell_0=d_G$ on $X_n$, where $G_k$ is the region graph (regions adjacent iff exactly one line separates them) and $G_k[X_n]$ its induced subgraph.

For the line-arrangement family with $k$ directions, $N_k(v):=\sum_j|\langle a_j,v\rangle|$ satisfies $N_k(v)=\tfrac{2k^2}{\pi}|v|\,(1+\varepsilon_k(v))$ with $|\varepsilon_k(v)|<4/k$, and $N_k(p-p')$ approximates $d_G(R,R')$ with error $<k$ for $p\in R$, $p'\in R'$ off the lines.

For the line-arrangement family (half-plane records, not local records; patterns with unboundedly many orbits) with $k_n\to\infty$ and $s_n=2k_n^2n/\pi$: $(X_n,\ell_0/s_n)$ converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to the Euclidean body $(B,|\cdot|_2)$ for the fixed compact convex $B$ with interior, and so does $(X_n,\ell/(\lambda s_n))$ for every $\lambda\in(0,\pi/2)$: continuum-like, of dimension 2, isotropic.

open_issues: 1(b), non-commuting X, Y: which of the (22.10) chains are ℓ-geodesics at fixed small λ depends on O(λ²) terms of α, not on d₀.

2(b), 3(a): the uniform remainder estimate (22.3) gives only sufficient small-λ bounds; in 2(b), with the margins (22.23), these bounds shrink exponentially with n, and for 3(a) the margins are not computed here; the actual stability thresholds of the neighbour graphs, including whether they have an n-independent lower bound, are not determined, and neither are the fixed-λ neighbour graphs for large n.

3(b): (22.29) and (22.32) rely on (P1)–(P3) as standard results and on (F1)–(F4); not determined (Step 10 (iii)): patterns with uniformly bounded orbit counts for which (F4) fails; truncations that create new edges at the boundary; whether local records, rather than the half-plane records of (22.36), can give an isotropic limit on patterns with growing cells.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions: α and ℓ are angles, λd₀ and λℓ₀ are dimensionless because K carries the inverse unit of λ, d₀ and ℓ₀ scale with σ in 1(a)–(b), and only λr₀ enters the case distinction in 1(c).

Small λ: the window angles (22.14) satisfy α/λ → √(2k) with k = min(r, m) for index distance r, which is (15.17); for the qubit disc d₀ is Euclidean, as in (22.5) with unit standard deviations and zero covariance, and it matches the λr₀ → 0 limit of (22.13) rescaled by 1/λ.

Limit q → 0 of 2(b) against m = 1: (22.19) tends to √2 for all r ≥ 1, which is (15.17) with m = 1, where (22.15) gives the complete graph through ties; the path graph (22.20) does not tend to it, consistent with the margins (22.23) vanishing as q → 0, since the neighbour relation is not continuous where its margins vanish.
